subject: POC scope & success criteria — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@acmecorp.com>, Priya Patel <priya.patel@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-28T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: POC scope and success criteria — next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for a productive discovery call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned before we spin up the POC: 

1) Confirmed primary use cases:
   - Semantic search over internal docs (docs + KB).
   - Real-time support summarization (agent -> chat history summarization for handoff).

2) Proposed success criteria (initial):
   - Semantic search: top-3 MRR precision >= 78% on your eval set; median embedding latency < 50ms (per request).
   - Support summarization: average ROUGE-L >= 0.45 vs. your labeled summaries; end-to-end latency < 200ms.

3) Timeline (proposed):
   - Start POC: week of Oct 5 (4-week run).
   - Week 0: onboarding + dataset access; Week 1: integration + baseline; Weeks 2-3: optimization & testing; Week 4: QA + wrap.

4) Ownership:
   - Customer: Alex (product lead) — dataset + success criteria signoff
   - Redwood: Marissa — POC coordination; Dylan — SE lead for integration

5) Next steps
   - Can you confirm the use cases above and whether the Oct 5 start works?
   - I attached a draft evaluation plan (ACME_POC_eval_plan_v1.pdf) with suggested metrics and checkpoints.

If that all looks reasonable I’ll kick off the setup ticket and schedule the onboarding call for next week.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: POC scope and success criteria — next steps

Thanks Marissa —

Quick responses from our side: we agree on semantic search and support summarization. Two asks/changes before we sign off: 

1) Add one more use case to the POC: content moderation classification for incoming user-generated content. We want to evaluate automated flags + human-in-loop workflow.

2) For moderation success criteria we’d like to aim for false negative rate < 2% on your model outputs (we’ll provide a labeled sample).

3) Timeline: due to internal scheduling, can we shift the start by one week (target Oct 12)? That gives us time to prepare the sample datasets.

Also, can you share an estimate of credits/pricing for a 4-week POC with a dedicated SE? I’ve attached our internal requirements spreadsheet (ACME_requirements.xlsx).

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Gomez
Sr. Product Manager, Acme Corp
alex.gomez@acmecorp.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-09-28T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC scope and success criteria — next steps

Alex — great, thanks for the clarity. We can absolutely add moderation as a third use case. A few notes and a proposed re-baseline below so we’re explicit about deliverables and expectations.

Revised proposal (v2):
- Start date: Oct 12, 2026
- Duration: 5 weeks (to accommodate additional use-case and evaluation time)
- Deliverables:
   * Integration + ingestion pipeline for your datasets
   * Baseline model runs for search, summarization, moderation
   * Weekly checkpoint metrics and one mid-POC tuning cycle
   * Final evaluation report and recommendations

Updated success criteria (suggested):
- Semantic search: top-3 precision >= 78% on your eval set; median embedding latency < 60ms
- Support summarization: ROUGE-L >= 0.45; 95th perc latency < 250ms
- Moderation: false negative rate <= 2.5% on the shared labeled sample (we recommend 2.5% as a pragmatic target given deployment delta; can discuss tightening with more labeled data)

Notes/asks for you:
- Please confirm dataset access method (S3 + service account preferred) and sample size for moderation labels (recommended >= 5k labeled items).
- We’ll include one dedicated SRE/SE session in week 1 and weekly 30-min checkpoints thereafter. If you want additional hands-on tuning we can add hours as a scoped add-on.

I attached v2 of the evaluation plan (ACME_POC_eval_plan_v2.pdf) with the above reflected. If you confirm the dataset access and the Oct 12 start we’ll kick off SSO + infra provisioning and send an updated SOW for signatures.

Also looping in Rishi / Dylan for any technical constraints or budget questions.

Thanks —
Marissa

Attachment: ACME_POC_eval_plan_v2.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: FW: ACME — POC rebaseline request

Forwarding Alex’s note — they want to add moderation and shift start to Oct 12, and they asked about credits/pricing. High level questions:
- Can we support a moderated use case with the proposed false-negative target (2.5% / Alex requested 2%) given the dataset likely size?
- Would we be comfortable extending to a 5-week POC and including a dedicated SE/SRE slot (we should define hours)?
- Finance: can we offer a small credit to close (they’re a strategic mid-market target)? Marcus — can you confirm any constraints on offering a $5k credit for POC trials?

Dylan — any tech notes on annotation volume / labeling needed and recommended model variant?

—Marissa
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-28T17:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: ACME — POC rebaseline request

Quick thoughts —
- Moderation is feasible but success depends heavily on labeled sample coverage (edge cases / multilingual). If Acme can provide >=5k labeled examples that reflect production traffic, hitting ~2% FNR is realistic with our recommended model (redwood-moderate-1.2b with safety-tuning).
- We'll need to reserve slightly more GPU capacity in week 2 for tuning runs; estimate ~24 GPU hours total spread across tuning.
- Recommend we include 40 hours of SE/SRE support across the POC (onboarding + tuning + two deep-dive sessions).

If Finance is okay with a $5k credit that nets them an attractive price and helps close, I’m supportive.

— Dylan

Agreed POC re-baseline:
- Start: Oct 12, 2026
- Duration: 5 weeks
- Use cases: semantic search, support summarization, moderation classification
- Success criteria: moderation FNR <= 2.5% (target), search/summarization metrics as in ACME_POC_eval_plan_v2.pdf

- Confirm dataset delivery method (S3 + service account preferred) and share initial labeled moderation sample (>=5k rows if possible).
- Sign the SOW once I send the draft (DocuSign link will follow).

I’ve attached the v2 evaluation plan and a draft SOW (ACME_SOW_draft.docx). Once you confirm dataset access and sign the SOW we’ll schedule the onboarding session for Oct 12.
